claims.claim: Moscrop says Written on the Dark is equally impressive for its accessibility and its density.
claims.source: David Moscrop, review of Written on the Dark, The Globe and Mail, 2025
claims.quote: equally as impressive for its accessibility and its density

claims.claim: Moscrop opens his review by citing the closing words of Written on the Dark.
claims.source: David Moscrop, review of Written on the Dark, The Globe and Mail, 2025
claims.quote: the closing words of Written on the Dark

claims.claim: The closing words of Written on the Dark, as Moscrop quotes them, are a four-word sentence repeated once.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay's novel Written on the Dark, closing words quoted by David Moscrop in The Globe and Mail, 2025
claims.quote: I did that. I did that.

claims.claim: Moscrop says the novel makes sense even for the mysteries it refuses to explain.
claims.source: David Moscrop, review of Written on the Dark, The Globe and Mail, 2025
claims.quote: even for the mysteries it refuses to explain
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'The brilliance of Written on the Dark'

claims.claim: Fram calls Kay a master of telling small stories in a big world.
claims.source: Noah Fram, starred review of All the Seas of the World, BookPage, 2022
claims.quote: A master of telling small stories in a big world

claims.claim: Fram says Kay's characters see their homes fade from the map and their lives taken for the pettiest of causes.
claims.source: Noah Fram, starred review of All the Seas of the World, BookPage, 2022
claims.quote: see their homes fade from the map

claims.claim: Wilt reports Kay saying his seniority frees him from the modern rule against jumping from past tense to present tense.
claims.source: Haley Byrd Wilt, 'The Author Who Pulled Me out of the Doomscroll', Christianity Today, 2025 (reporter's paraphrase of Kay's remarks)
claims.quote: Don’t jump from the past tense to the present tense
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'It helps that Kay'

claims.claim: Wilt reports Kay naming the rule against hopping between characters' heads as one he does not have to obey.
claims.source: Haley Byrd Wilt, 'The Author Who Pulled Me out of the Doomscroll', Christianity Today, 2025 (reporter's paraphrase of Kay's remarks)
claims.quote: just choose one perspective per chapter
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'It helps that Kay'

claims.claim: Wilt reports Kay naming the rule against writing a whole chapter from the viewpoint of a plot-irrelevant medieval courier.
claims.source: Haley Byrd Wilt, 'The Author Who Pulled Me out of the Doomscroll', Christianity Today, 2025 (reporter's paraphrase of Kay's remarks)
claims.quote: an entire chapter from the viewpoint of a grizzled medieval courier
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'It helps that Kay'

claims.claim: Kay says simply that he trusts his readers.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed in Toronto by Haley Byrd Wilt, Christianity Today, 2025
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Still, Kay has resisted'

claims.claim: Kay says every book he has written has been in part an attempt to look at how different and how similar the past is.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed in Toronto by Haley Byrd Wilt, Christianity Today, 2025
claims.quote: how different the past is and how similar it is
claims.page: body, quotation beginning 'Every book I've ever written'

claims.claim: Kay characterises the people of the past with concrete wants: security, a roof, a harvest.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed in Toronto by Haley Byrd Wilt, Christianity Today, 2025
claims.quote: wanted security, wanted a roof, wanted a harvest
claims.page: body, quotation beginning 'The people of the past are strange'

claims.claim: Wilt says there are no elaborate, concrete magic systems in Kay's books, which are instead haunted by the transcendent.
claims.source: Haley Byrd Wilt, 'The Author Who Pulled Me out of the Doomscroll', Christianity Today, 2025 (reporter's paraphrase of Kay's remarks)
claims.quote: There are no elaborate, concrete magic systems here

claims.claim: Kay states that when writers work with distant history they are, to a great degree, guessing.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'Home and Away', BrightWeavings (speech, amended; short version Globe and Mail 1999)
claims.page: body, paragraph on The Lions of Al-Rassan and Rodrigo Diaz

claims.claim: Kay says inventing a setting and a character modelled on a real figure demonstrates a measure of appropriate distance.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'Home and Away', BrightWeavings
